newsitem.title: UK: Medeva acquires nicotine treatment rights.
newsitem.headline: Medeva acquires nicotine treatment rights.

text.p: Drug company Medeva Plc said on Wednesday it had acquired an exclusive worldwide licence to all rights relating to the manufacture and use of all forms of nicotine in the treatment of gastro-intestinal diseases.
These rights were acquired under the pending patent filed by Mayo Clinic, Medeva said in a statement.

It said an estimated 300,000 people in the U.S. and a similar number in Europe suffer from ulcerative colitis which it described as "a chronic gastro-intestinal disease which is not adequately treated by current medications".

Medeva said it had patented technology in the field of drug delivery systems for use in the treatment of lower gastro-intestinal diseases through its acquisition of Tillotts. The agreement with Mayo Clinic "provides an extension to Medeva's development portfolio in this area", it added.

Under the terms of the licence, Medeva said it will pay Mayo Cinic -- a large U.S. private medicine group practice -- "initial milestone payments, the substantial part of which can be credited against royalties on future sales of product".

Medeva said studies by Mayo Clinic in the U.S. and at the University Hospital in Wales showed nicotine patches had therapeutic benefits in the treatment of ulcerative colitis, but there were also unacceptable side-effects in some patients.

Studies conducted at the same time in the same institutions had shown, however, that nicotine complexed with a carbomer and delivered by enema "did not produce significant systemic blood levels and caused minimal side-effects", it said.
In a study of 22 patients, this method led to 75 percent of the group showing improvement after eight weeks of therapy, including 23 percent going into complete remission, it said.
